title: Titila, the Shy Shooting Star
summary: A shy little star doesn't dare to cross the sky, afraid she'll grant the wrong wish.

scenes.text:
High up in the night lived a little star named Titila. Every night, trailing tails of light across the sky, went all the other stars.

Down below, sleeping children made their wishes. And waving to every one of them, round and kind, was the Moon. But Titila stayed still in her corner, glowing very softly.

She loved to watch the sleeping world down below: the rooftops, the trees, and the rivers. She dreamed of crossing the sky one day... but just thinking about it made her light tremble a bit.

She still didn't dare.

Why was Titila so afraid? She thought: 'What if a child makes a wish and I get it wrong? What if they ask for a hug and I give them a balloon?

' Just imagining it, she hid behind a cloud. One night her face was stroked by a warm wind. 'It's alright, little one.

Nobody wishes for perfect wishes,' it whispered.

But shy Titila closed her eyes and kept trembling in silence. She would rather watch from far away, where no one could see her cross.

That very night, her trembling was seen by the Moon. In her soft voice, she asked, 'Little Titila, why do you never cross the sky? ' From a branch, with big round eyes, listened an old owl.

Very quietly, Titila confessed her secret: 'I'm afraid of giving a child the wrong wish. ' She smiled the slow, wide smile that only clear nights have. 'Oh, my little star,' she said.

'Come closer. Let me tell you how wishes really work. ' And curious Titila floated just a little bit nearer.

'Wishes don't live inside you,' said the Moon. 'They live in the one who dreams, deep down in the heart.

You only carry your light; the child brings the wish. You can never get it wrong, because you give away shine, not orders. ' Titila thought about it slowly.

She filled herself with air and breathed. It felt like filling up with courage. From her branch, someone hooted softly, as if to say, 'You can do it.

' For the first time, the little star felt her fear was tiny, the size of a crumb. And quietly inside, a little spark of bravery began to grow.

Then, at last, Titila dared. She spread her wings of light and, from one end of the sky to the other, she crossed.

Behind her she left a soft golden tail. Down below, a half-asleep girl saw her through the window. She made a tiny wish and whispered.

Titila never knew what it was... and she understood it didn't matter. The girl smiled and snuggled into her bed.

A little wink came from the Moon. And Titila, peaceful now, drifted back to her corner to rest, glowing softly. Good night, little star.

Good night. Time to sleep.
